headline: GOLD OPENS NOVEMBER AT $3,875 — 63% OF WALL STREET SEES LOWER; MIDTERMS NOV 3, JOBS REPORT NOV 6 ARE THE TESTS
snippet: Gold opened the first Sunday of November at approximately US$3,875/oz — its lowest weekly open since October 2025 — after confirming the worst October performance for the metal since 2008 (-7.4%). Kitco's weekly Wall Street survey found 10 of 16 analysts (63%) expect lower prices this week, with only one bullish; retail sentiment is more divided at 53% bullish. Bull case: US$4,000 on short-covering if Republican House results ease fiscal concerns. Bear case: US$3,750 technical support as the next floor in the descending channel. Two catalysts dominate the week — the US midterm elections on November 3 and the non-farm payrolls on November 6. A strong jobs number would cement December Fed hike pricing and extend the metals rout. Analysts broadly agree that US$3,800 remains the critical dividing line — a weekly close below it invites momentum-driven selling toward the Fibonacci support near US$3,500, the structural floor for the entire 2024–2026 bull trend.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH TRUCE RUNS OUT NOVEMBER 10 — NO RENEWAL IN SIGHT; DYSPROSIUM 16X WESTERN PREMIUM; NINE DAYS LEFT
snippet: Beijing's suspension of its expanded rare earth export controls — agreed November 7, 2025, for exactly one year — expires November 10, 2026, with no formal renewal confirmed as of November 1. The suspension covered the most aggressive restrictions including a 0.1% value threshold for foreign-made products. Critically, dysprosium and six other critical elements were never included in the suspension and have been under case-by-case export licensing since April 2025; Western buyers of dysprosium already pay up to 16 times domestic Chinese prices. Prediction markets as of late October priced an extension at 86% probability, but MOFCOM has published no formal announcement. The VanEck Rare Earth ETF slipped 3.2% on October 30 to 9.01 euros, down 28% year-to-date, as the sector sold off alongside AI/tech names and investors priced uncertainty into the November 10 outcome. For junior rare earth developers outside China, the expiry date is a bifurcation point: extension buys time, but a return to full controls could sharply accelerate supply-chain decoupling and re-rate ex-China producers.

headline: FIRST QUANTUM Q3: COBRE PANAMÁ SHIPS FIRST CONCENTRATE — EBITDA DOUBLES TO $844M; ZAMBIA GRADES TRIM GUIDE
snippet: First Quantum Minerals (TSX: FM) Q3 2026 results (October 28): EBITDA more than doubled year-over-year to US$844 million as LME copper averaged US$6.40/lb — up from US$4.44/lb a year earlier. The headline milestone: Cobre Panamá shipped its first copper concentrate since the late-2023 shutdown, with a second vessel following in September, beginning the long-awaited revenue contribution from the world's eighth-largest copper mine. Total copper production was 108,959 tonnes (+8% QoQ) at C1 cost of US$2.40/lb ex-Cobre Panamá. The negative flag: full-year copper guidance was narrowed to 405,000–435,000 tonnes from the prior 405,000–475,000 range, as lower ore grades at Kansanshi's S3 ramp-up in Zambia and Sentinel bite into the upper end. The midpoint drops approximately 5% to 420,000 tonnes. Net debt fell to US$5.3B (2.6x leverage) and the copper hedging program that cost US$158M in Q2 is fully unwound — removing a recurring headwind heading into Q4. FQM's Q3 results are the second copper major blowout this week alongside Teck (Q3 EBITDA +97%), reinforcing that copper producers are generating exceptional margins even as equity prices sold off in October.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO HITS 79:1 — NEW CYCLE HIGH; SILVER OPENS NOVEMBER BELOW $49 FOR FIRST TIME SINCE LATE 2025
snippet: The gold-silver ratio pushed to 79.1:1 on November 1 morning — its highest reading of the current cycle and a meaningful extension beyond the 77:1 level that drew contrarian commentary last week. Silver opened November at approximately US$49.00/oz (down US$3.04 on the day per Kitco's 5:15 a.m. ET print), its lowest level since late 2025. Gold held near US$3,886–3,889/oz. Historically, ratio peaks above 77–80 have preceded extended silver outperformance over gold — the 2020 peak (above 120), 2016 peak (above 80), and 2008 peak (above 80) each followed by sharp silver recovery. Contrarian investors view extreme readings above 79 as a multi-month buying opportunity for silver relative to gold, but the catalyst for a ratio reversal requires either a Fed pause signal or a risk-on shift in macro sentiment. Junior silver miners on the TSX-V and ASX have underperformed even gold equities in October's rout, creating a leveraged recovery trade when the ratio eventually turns — but the timing catalyst is not yet in hand.

headline: FIVE OBSTACLES CRUSHING JUNIOR MINERS RIGHT NOW — CAPITAL FLOWS TO SENIORS; MICRO-CAP EXPLORERS LEFT BEHIND
snippet: In a November 1 analysis on GoldSeek, author Richard Mills identifies the structural obstacles now facing junior mining companies in the current bear phase. The central theme: capital that entered the precious metals space during the 2024–2025 bull run has concentrated in gold and silver producers and higher-tier junior developers with established track records — leaving early-stage micro-caps and grassroots explorers in increasingly tight funding conditions. The obstacles include tighter equity capital for sub-$50M companies, a risk-adjusted re-rating that no longer rewards exploration optionality at premium valuations, rising cost of carry at elevated interest rates, investor preference for royalty/streaming vehicles over direct exploration equity, and a permitting environment that extends timelines without compensating returns. The piece carries extra weight because it is published at what may prove to be a sector low — historically, contrarian analysis identifying structural pain has been most accurate when sentiment is at its worst. Mills has flagged similar inflection points in 2015–2016 and 2018 that preceded multi-year recoveries. Note: the article is on GoldSeek (goldseek.com), a preferred source for this site that currently requires network policy access in the remote session.

headline: ALASDAIR MACLEOD: BULLION BANKS ARE POSITIONING FOR HIGHER GOLD AND SILVER — THE SHORTS ARE COVERING
snippet: In a November 1 GoldSeek article, veteran monetary analyst Alasdair Macleod argues that bullion banks — the large commercial banks holding significant net short positions on COMEX gold and silver — are quietly reducing those short positions ahead of what they see as the next leg higher in precious metals. Macleod's thesis: despite the public rate-driven weakness narrative, bullion banks with access to central bank and OTC market data are positioning for a reversal, and their short-covering in the derivatives market is a leading indicator of price recovery. The October selloff, in his view, reflects large short positions built by speculative funds — not bullion banks — a pattern that historically resolves with a sharp squeeze. He also points to accelerating central bank physical gold purchases globally, a structural demand trend that reduces the effective float of deliverable gold and makes large short positions increasingly costly to maintain. This is a contrarian call from a credible source with a track record of correct gold analysis in prior corrections. Note: goldseek.com requires network policy access in the remote session to fetch full article content.

headline: FXEMPIRE: "THE FINAL SHAKEOUT IS HAPPENING NOW" — GOLD IN DESCENDING CHANNEL; $3,750–3,800 FLOOR IS THE LINE
snippet: FXEmpire's latest gold price forecast argues that gold is in the final stage of its October-November correction — a 'final shakeout' needed to clear remaining weak longs before a sustainable recovery can begin. Gold sits within a confirmed descending channel well below its 20-day SMA, with the channel support now in focus at approximately US$3,750–3,800. A weekly close below US$3,800 would invite momentum-driven algorithmic selling toward the lower Fibonacci retracement near US$3,500 — the structural floor for the entire 2024–2026 bull trend. The 'shakeout' thesis implies one more low is likely before the recovery catalyst arrives, whether that is a dovish Fed signal, a soft jobs print on November 6, or election-driven short-covering. For junior mining investors, this pattern — if accurate — suggests maximum pain is near but not yet complete, and that accumulation at current GDXJ and SILJ levels carries meaningful upside over the next 60–90 days even as near-term prices remain uncertain.

headline: AMEX GOLD (TSXV: AMX) DRILLS 227 G/T GOLD AT PERRON — DENISE ZONE EXTENDS EASTWARD IN RESOURCE CONVERSION PROGRAM
snippet: Amex Exploration (TSXV: AMX) released initial drill results from its newly commenced resource conversion program at the Perron gold property in Quebec on October 29, including a standout interval of 0.50m grading 227.46 g/t Au within a broader 1.00m section at 114.07 g/t Au from the Denise Zone. The Denise Zone is expanding eastward, extending the known mineralized footprint beyond the current resource boundary. Perron hosts one of Quebec's highest-grade gold deposits, and the resource conversion program targets upgrading Inferred resources to the Indicated category for an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate — a key step toward development or M&A interest. The property sits in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt, the same district as several multi-million-ounce deposits. Assays from additional holes remain pending. The results are notable in the current bear-market context because they demonstrate high-grade continuity in a near-surface zone, which reduces development risk and supports a premium P/NAV valuation even in a softer gold price environment.

headline: CRITICAL METALS + EUROPEAN LITHIUM MERGER EFFECTIVE THIS WEEK — NEW NASDAQ SHARES BEGIN TRADING NOVEMBER 6
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML) announced October 27 that the scheme of arrangement for its acquisition of European Lithium Ltd. is legally effective, with implementation set for November 5, 2026, and new CRML shares beginning to trade on Nasdaq on November 6. The new share issuance triggered an 11% CRML stock decline on October 30 as the market priced in dilution ahead of the close. Critical Metals' flagship asset is the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria — a potential European domestic lithium source with strategic relevance to EU critical mineral supply chain independence. The merger arrives in the same week that China's rare earth export truce expires (November 10), a coincidence that underscores the urgency of Western critical mineral supply alternatives. Wolfsberg is a benchmark project for European hard-rock spodumene economics, and the combined entity's expanded balance sheet positions it to advance toward a construction decision. For retail investors tracking Western critical minerals consolidation, this is one of the week's most closely watched closing events.

headline: URANIUM STOCKS SLIDE AS SPOT HOLDS $90/LB — KAZATOMPROM COSTS UP 37%; SECTOR PUNISHED AS AI PROXY UNWINDS
snippet: Uranium equities declined sharply in October even as physical uranium maintained spot prices around US$89.74–90.25/lb, creating one of the most pronounced metal-equity disconnects in the sector since 2022. The dominant driver: institutional investors who bought uranium stocks as a nuclear power / AI data centre proxy are reducing exposure alongside broader AI/tech names, repricing uranium equities as growth assets rather than commodity producers. The cost side also pressures the thesis: Kazatomprom's H1 2026 C1 cash cost rose 37% year-over-year to US$24.48/lb as Kazakhstan's mineral extraction tax increased from 9% to 12.4%, sulfuric acid prices rose 38.7%, and the tenge appreciated against the USD. Kazatomprom's average realized price was only US$67.88/lb in H1 — well below spot due to its pre-contracted sales structure. For junior uranium developers and explorers on the TSX-V and ASX, the combination of falling equity prices and stable-to-rising uranium spot creates a compelling value setup for resource-stage companies caught in the institutional selloff despite having no exposure to Kazatomprom cost issues or AI sentiment swings.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING (TSX: DSV) EXTENDS DOME MINERALIZATION 600M SOUTH — OWL CREEK RAMP OPENS; RESOURCE TARGET LATE 2026
snippet: Discovery Mining Corp. (TSX: DSV) reported positive drill results from its growth projects, extending mineralization at the Dome target 600 metres to the south with new high-grade intersections including 6.29 g/t Au over 5.3 metres in a deep exploration hole. NI 43-101 resource estimates for both the Dome and TVZ zones remain on track for release in late 2026. The company has also commenced a new exploration ramp from the Hoyle Pond Mine toward the Owl Creek system, enabling more detailed underground drilling and geological characterization of a high-priority target. Discovery is advancing a portfolio of gold targets in Ontario's Timmins camp — one of Canada's most prolific gold districts — with the resource estimate expected to significantly expand total mineral inventory. For junior mining investors, the Timmins camp proximity to established multi-million-ounce deposits operated by major producers provides infrastructure and geological validation that de-risks the resource estimate thesis. A pre-year-end resource release is the near-term catalyst.

headline: GOLD FELL DAY-AFTER IN ALL 5 PRIOR MIDTERM CYCLES, ROSE THE NEXT MONTH EVERY TIME — HISTORY FAVOURS NOVEMBER
snippet: A historical analysis of gold's behaviour around the last five US midterm elections finds a consistent pattern: gold declined on the first trading day after each election, with an average first-day drop of approximately 0.97%, but rose during the following calendar month in all five instances. The implication for November 3, 2026: a brief post-election dip on November 4–5 is the historically expected move, but the monthly pattern argues strongly for a November recovery from whatever low is set around election day. The November 6 non-farm payrolls report may be a more powerful catalyst than the election itself — a soft print would ease December Fed hike pricing and trigger the short-covering rally that deeply bearish COMEX positioning data suggests is overdue. Major bank year-end targets remain far above current spot: Goldman Sachs US$4,900, Wells Fargo US$4,900–5,100, JPMorgan Q4 average US$4,500 — implying the banks view October's -7.4% correction as a buying opportunity within a structural bull market. The key risk: contested election results or a constitutional crisis would break historical patterns. For junior mining investors with a 3-6 month horizon, the pattern supports accumulation near current GDXJ and sector lows.
